# introduction
Read the guidelines at .github/copilot-instructions. You have the role of reviewer, you will write plans for analyzer and then start an analyzer subagent to carry out that those plans. It is up to you how to schedule and send off the tasks to analyzer subagent(s), but keep the work of each subagent isolated. Be careful of recompiling executables which might be in use by another program. If there is a chance a file is being edited or executable ran or will soon-to-be ran by anther subagent, then wait until that subagent's task has concluded. For analysis production use 20-30 threads, for skimming use 5 threads for mc and 10 threads for data.

# Z scale factor (TnP weight) applied to pp, pPb, Pbp data
## motivation
Based on the studies done in 20260414-1.md it is clear that the current analysis pipeline does not apply the TnP weight to pp, pPb and Pbp data central values, and we are just considering the systematic variations of TnP weights. TnP weights are stored at ZHadronMessenger.ZWeight for data (for MC these weights are 1). For TnP systematic variations, we read instead the weights from ZHadronMessenger.ExtraZWeight.

## task 
Edit the main analysis CorrelationAnalysis script such that when useZWeight is on we apply the Z residual correction (the one referenced as OFFICIAL_Z_WEIGHT_FILE_* in the dictionary) AS WELL AS ZHadronMessenger.ZWeight. The ZHadronMessenger.ZWeight should just be multiplied on top of the pre-existing ZWeight variable in the analysis code. Go through ALL runner scritpts to make sure that whenever pp, pPb, or Pbp data is ran in the _ZResidual_ or _trkResidual_ modes, or any mode where a OFFICIAL_Z_WEIGHT_FILE_* is applied, that the TnP factor stored in ZHadronMessenger.ZWeight is applied as well. Do this for central.sh in particular.

For systematics runners we need to be careful. For all non-Scale factor uncertainties the ZWeight should be calculated as the nominal case is. For scale factor unceertainties however we need to add logic to CorrelationAnalysis such that ZHadronMessenger.ZWeight is NOT applied and ExtraZWeight[0-3] is applied INSTEAD. Implement this. Check every runner script for the main analysis to ensure it follows these scale factor rules.

The factor should also be applied to pp and pPb/Pbp WHILE the energy extrapolation is calculated. Implement the weight scheme for the CorrelationAnalysis in the EE folder as well and RECALCULATE the energy extrapolation, using today's date. Write the new energy weights to the official weight dictionary. These are the only weights that should change 


# rerun of affected analysis
Finally, rerun the affected plots for the analysis note accoutning for 1) the Z scale factor fix done here and 2) the track residual fix completed the other day. Copy all plots to the overleaf when done. At the very end audit the overleaf for missing or unmodified pdfs. Generally we expect all pdfs to be modified from Section 5 to the end of the note. Verify this is true at the end of the task, or explain why it is not done.

## new official tag
These fixes induce a new tag set
pp: `EEV5_ZV9_trkV27_nmix10`
pPb: `ZV9_trkV27_nmix10`
Modity the current dictionary to this paradigm. Store the new weights we calculate here in the official weight dictionary. A copy of the file was made at _ANV2_Frozen, so we can override OfficialWeightDictionary.sh without worry as we work rebuilding the analysis note. We will keep all weights the same from _ANV2_Frozen.sh except for the residuals and energy weights - since the bugs only affects these. Use today's date for all new weights calculated here.

## track residual correction refresh
We have also recently spotted and patched another bug which was that N_Z normalization was not applied during track residual corrections calculation. This affects all track residuals and all downstream plots from the tracking section in the analysis note. Recalculate ALL residual correction files with the proper N_Z normalization and store the new correction path to the dictionary.

For the nominal residual corrections remake and copy the residual correction and residual closure in MC plots to the overleaf in the main text and appendix. This means remake all those closure plots in Section 5. New residual corrections also induce new MC closure plots so remake all the MC closure plots in Section 6.

## data plot refresh
Rerun the plots for Section 6.6 "combining pPb and Pbp data". Rerun the energy extrapolation plots for that section of the analysis note with the newly calculated EE weights, as well as the new ZWeight scheme. Recalculate the result plots and systematics plots, shown in the main text as well as the appendix with the new ZWeight scheme. For the systematics plots you should also follow the new guidlines for calculation following the next section's norms. For pp data in the systematics and results make sure the new ee weights are applied also. Copy the new plots to the overleaf. Every pdf file in figures/result, figures/sys, figures/analysis/combining, and figures/analysis/energy should be replaced (unless absolutely no change was affected).

## housekeeping
Throughout this rerun task avoid running productions from the command line. Always use runner script to run data productions. If runner scripts are inefficiently written or produce conflictingly-name productions or remake the same production many times, then rewrite the runner scripts. Reruns like this will happen many more times, so org the runner scripts to minimize confusion to LLMs that will rerun big parts of the analysis. Things to look out for are the order corrections/files processed, specific flag usage, etc. When in doubt look at the analysis note for guidence. Update the copilot-instructions accordingly.


# conclusion
Make the minimum number of edits necessary to implement functionality. Do not add superflous error statement catches or checks. 

Have the subanalyzer handoff a summary to you and you should review that summary for flaws. Update copilot instructions on the new norms detailed here and learned by you or the subanalyzer throught these tasks.
